questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph represents:
questions.explanation:
The area under a velocity-time graph represents displacement because it is equal to
velocity × time.

questions.question: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². The displacement in 5 seconds is:
questions.explanation:
Using equation of motion: s = ut + 1/2 at²
Here u = 0, a = 2, t = 5
s = 1/2 × 2 × 25 = 25 m

questions.question: In projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity:
questions.explanation:
Horizontal velocity remains constant because there is no acceleration in horizontal
direction (ignoring air resistance).

questions.question: At the maximum height of a projectile, its vertical velocity is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, vertical velocity becomes zero.

questions.question: The trajectory of a projectile is a:
questions.explanation:
Projectile motion follows a parabolic path due to constant gravity and uniform horizontal
motion.

questions.question: A ball is thrown horizontally from a height. Its vertical acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Only gravity acts vertically, so vertical acceleration is 9.8 m/s² downward.

questions.question: The range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is:
questions.explanation: Range is maximum at 45° because sin(2θ) becomes 1.

questions.question: Which pair of angles will result in the same range for a projectile launched with the same speed?
questions.explanation: Angles 35° and 55° are complementary (sum = 90°), giving same range.

questions.question: The time of flight of a projectile is given by the formula:
questions.explanation: Time of flight = 2u sinθ / g

questions.question: If a projectile is launched at 90°, its range will be:
questions.explanation: At 90°, motion is vertical so horizontal range is zero.

questions.question: Newton’s second law of motion is mathematically expressed as:
questions.explanation: Newton’s second law: F = ma

questions.question: The SI unit of impulse is:
questions.explanation: Impulse unit is Newton-second or kg m/s.

questions.question: A change in momentum is known as:
questions.explanation: Impulse is change in momentum.

questions.question: The law of conservation of momentum is valid in:
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved only in isolated systems.

questions.question: In an elastic collision, which quantity is NOT conserved?

options.D: None of the above (all are conserved)

questions.explanation: In elastic collisions, momentum and kinetic energy both are conserved.

questions.question: In a perfectly inelastic collision, the objects:
questions.explanation: In perfectly inelastic collision, objects stick together.

questions.question: The slope of a displacement-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope of displacement-time graph gives velocity.

questions.question: If the velocity-time graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis, the acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Zero slope means zero acceleration (constant velocity).

questions.question: A 1 kg mass moving at 10 m/s has a momentum of:
questions.explanation: Momentum = mv = 1 × 10 = 10 kg m/s

questions.question: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils because of:
questions.explanation: Gun recoils due to conservation of momentum.

questions.question: For a projectile, the maximum height reached is:
questions.explanation: Maximum height depends on square of vertical velocity component.

questions.question: If air resistance is considered, the range of a projectile:
questions.explanation: Air resistance reduces range.

questions.question: An object thrown at 45° has a range R. What is its range if thrown at 135°?
questions.explanation: Angles 45° and 135° give same range (theoretical symmetry).

questions.question: The rate of change of momentum is equal to:
questions.explanation: Rate of change of momentum equals force.

questions.question: A body of mass m is moving with velocity v. If the mass is doubled and velocity is halved, the momentum:
questions.explanation: Momentum remains same when mass doubles and velocity halves.

questions.question: Friction is a force that always:
questions.explanation: Friction always opposes relative motion.

questions.question: A ball is dropped from a height h. Its velocity just before hitting the ground is:
Which law of motion explains the “jerk” forward when a bus suddenly stops?
questions.explanation: Sudden stopping shows inertia (Newton’s first law).

questions.question: The product of mass and velocity is:
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity.

questions.question: If two bodies of different masses have the same momentum, the lighter body will have:
questions.explanation: Lighter body has more kinetic energy when momentum is same.

questions.question: The acceleration of a body moving with constant velocity is:
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration.

questions.question: In an elastic collision of two equal masses, where one is initially at rest:

options.D: The first one continues moving with double speed

questions.explanation: Equal masses exchange velocities in elastic collision.

questions.question: The engine of a car provides a constant force. The acceleration:
questions.explanation: Constant force gives constant acceleration.

questions.question: A projectile’s path is determined by:
questions.explanation: Projectile motion depends on gravity and inertia.

questions.question: The dimension of impulse is same as that of:
questions.explanation: Impulse has same dimension as momentum.

questions.question: The range of a projectile is same as the maximum height when tan θ is:
questions.explanation: Relation shows tanθ = 4 (from simplification).

questions.question: If the time of flight of a projectile is 4 seconds, the time taken to reach maximum height is:
questions.explanation: Time to reach max height is half of total flight time.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement is vector quantity.

questions.question: The area under a force-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Force-time graph area gives change in momentum.

questions.question: Rocket propulsion is based on:

options.C: Newton’s third law and conservation of momentum

questions.explanation: Rocket works on Newton’s third law and conservation of momentum.

questions.question: A body is moving in a circle with constant speed. Its velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity changes direction in circular motion.

questions.question: The distance covered by a body in time t starting from rest with acceleration a is:
questions.explanation: s = 1/2 at²

questions.question: When a force of 1 N acts on a mass of 1 kg, the acceleration is:
questions.explanation: a = F/m = 1/1 = 1 m/s²

questions.question: In a collision, the total energy is:
questions.explanation: Total energy is always conserved.

questions.question: A projectile is fired at 30°. If the launch speed is doubled, the range becomes:
questions.explanation: Range is proportional to square of velocity.

questions.question: The slope of the velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope of v-t graph gives acceleration.

questions.question: An object is moving with constant acceleration. The velocity-time graph is:
questions.explanation: Constant acceleration gives straight inclined line.

questions.question: If the net force on a body is zero, it must be:

options.C: Either at rest or moving with constant velocity

questions.explanation: Net force zero means rest or uniform motion.

questions.question: A passenger in a moving car tosses a coin vertically. The coin falls:
questions.explanation: Coin stays in hand due to inertia.

questions.question: The unit of force “Newton” in terms of base units is:
questions.explanation: Newton = kg m/s²

questions.question: Inertia of a body depends on its:
questions.explanation: Inertia depends on mass.

questions.question: During long jump, an athlete runs before jumping to:
questions.explanation: Athlete gains momentum for longer jump.

questions.question: A ball of mass m strikes a wall with velocity v and bounces back with same velocity. The change in momentum is:
questions.explanation: Change in momentum = 2mv

questions.question: A system is “isolated” if:

options.B: No external force acts on it

questions.explanation: No external force means isolated system.

questions.question: The ratio of displacement to distance is always:
questions.explanation: Displacement is always less than or equal to distance.

questions.question: A body thrown vertically upwards reaches a maximum height H. The total distance covered on returning to the starting point is:
questions.explanation: Total distance = 2H

questions.question: What remains constant for a projectile even in the presence of air resistance?
questions.explanation: With air resistance nothing remains strictly constant.

questions.question: The range of a projectile at 15° is 50 m. At 45°, the range will be:
questions.explanation: Range at 45° is double that at 15° case.

questions.question: For a body falling freely, the distance covered in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd seconds are in the ratio:
questions.explanation: Odd number ratio: 1 : 3 : 5

questions.question: If the mass of a projectile is doubled, its time of flight:
questions.explanation: Mass does not affect time of flight.

questions.question: A cricketer moves his hands backwards while catching a ball to:

options.C: Decrease the force by increasing the time of impact
options.D: Catch the ball at a higher point

questions.explanation: Increasing time reduces force (impulse concept).

questions.question: The coefficient of restitution for a perfectly elastic collision is:
questions.explanation: Elastic collision coefficient = 1

questions.question: When two bodies of equal mass undergo an elastic collision in 1-D, they:
questions.explanation: Equal masses exchange velocities.

questions.question: Maximum range R of a projectile is 100 m. Its maximum height H at this angle (45°) is:
questions.explanation: At 45°, maximum height is one-fourth of range.

questions.question: Velocity of a projectile at the maximum height is:
questions.explanation: Horizontal component remains at top.

questions.question: If the momentum of a body is increased by 20%, its kinetic energy increases by:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy increases by 44%

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of translatory motion?

options.A: A car moving on a road

questions.explanation: Spinning top is rotational motion.

questions.question: The angle between velocity and acceleration at the peak of a projectile’s path is:
questions.explanation: Velocity and acceleration are perpendicular at peak.

questions.question: A constant force acts on a 5 kg mass for 2 seconds, changing its velocity from 3 m/s to 7 m/s. The force is:
questions.explanation: F = ma = 10 N

questions.question: Displacement is defined as:
questions.explanation: Displacement is shortest straight-line distance.

questions.question: A body moves 3 m North and then 4 m East. The magnitude of displacement is:
questions.explanation: Pythagoras gives 5 m.

questions.question: A body is thrown vertically up with velocity u. The time to reach maximum height is:
questions.explanation: Time to max height = u/g

questions.question: The unit of momentum is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Momentum unit = N s

questions.question: If the collision is perfectly inelastic, the kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy is lost.

questions.question: The range of a projectile depends on:
questions.explanation: Range depends on all listed factors.

questions.question: An athlete can throw a javelin at a maximum distance of 100 m. How high can he throw it vertically?
questions.explanation: Vertical height = half of max range case

questions.question: Average velocity is defined as:
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement / time

questions.question: A car travels at 60 km/h for 1 hour and 40 km/h for the next hour. The average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed = 50 km/h

questions.question: Friction depends on:
questions.explanation: Friction depends on surface and normal force

questions.question: Two bodies of mass M and m (M > m) are dropped from the same height. In a vacuum, they will reach the ground:
questions.explanation: All bodies fall equally in vacuum
